# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Daily Update (Aug 7, 2026)

## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on addressing critical stability issues, particularly around sequencer failover and interop testing, with significant progress made on identifying root causes and proposing fixes for flaky tests. A new token was also proposed for integration on Base.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No completed work was reported for this period.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **New Token Integration**: A new pull request, [#1347](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1347), was opened to add the AAH (AliensAreHere) token on Base.

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Conductor System Coverage Porting**: Issue [#21902](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21902) was closed, indicating the porting of user-visible conductor behaviors from `op-e2e` to `op-acceptance-tests` and `op-devstack` DSL is complete. The underlying `op-conductor` availability bug is being tracked separately.
- **Post-Exec Transaction Validation**: Issue [#21961](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21961) was closed. It was determined that both `op-node` and Kona treat `PostExecTxs` as opaque bytes during derivation, with further validation being the responsibility of the Execution Layer.
- **Flaky Sequencer Failover Test Resolution**: The flaky test issue [#22094](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22094) (`TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC`) was closed. The fix involved removing the rapid back-to-back leadership transfer sequence from the test and replacing it with focused acceptance coverage, mitigating the high-probability reproducer for an underlying `op-conductor` availability bug.

## NEW ISSUES

No new issues were reported for this period.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **Flaky Supernode Light Sequencer Interop Test**: Issue [#22234](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22234) (`TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`) is being actively investigated. The latest comments indicate a root cause has been found: a real race in the test's final assertions, not an environmental failure. Two distinct failure signatures were identified:
    - **Signature A**: The `safe-label` gate does not stabilize by-number reads, leading to a transient disagreement between the light CL's divergent branch and the upstream branch, causing `AssertTxInBlock` to fail. A proposed fix involves replacing the `Reached(eth.Safe, N)` + single-shot `AssertTxInBlock(N)` with a retrying check that polls until the canonical block at N contains (or does not contain) the transaction.
    - **Signature B**: The `ResendUntilSafe` budget is exhausted under merge-queue load, indicating a genuine stall rather than slow progress. The cross-safe recovery pace is bounded, and the current budget is tight. A separate issue, [#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22325), has been created to investigate this cross-safety issue further, as cross-safe appears to stop following local-safe post-replacement. A draft PR, [#22321](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22321), is up for fixing Signature A.
